kind: observed events (ERCOT monthly Operations Reports, n=311) + two-stage model; extrapolation beyond observed range is MODELED
units: Hz nadir; MW loss; rates per year

stage2_nadir.formula: log(depth) = a + b log(MW) + c log(inertia GW*s) + d*years_since_2018-11 + eps; evaluated at yr_ref (latest observed)

conditional_nadir.distribution: Uniform(59.302, 59.58) Hz between the two documented events (2 data points: scenario-grade)

systemic_stress_regime.note: Rate evidence is 2 events / 14.7 years (credible interval wide); events defined as ERCOT cold-weather/scarcity emergencies with firm load shed. Earlier events (e.g. 1989) not used. In-regime nadir comes from 2 events only. Units: rate per year.

stress_scenarios_not_probabilistic.name: Winter Storm Uri 2021-02-15
stress_scenarios_not_probabilistic.fact: frequency below 59.4 Hz for 4 min 23 s; ~52 GW generation forced out (S&P Global reporting); NOT in event table

stress_scenarios_not_probabilistic.name: ERCOT largest single contingency
stress_scenarios_not_probabilistic.fact: 1,430 MW (ERCOT AS study 2024); RRS sized to keep frequency >=59.7 Hz

stress_scenarios_not_probabilistic.name: Two largest units
stress_scenarios_not_probabilistic.fact: ERCOT procures RRS to survive loss of two largest units and stay above 59.3 Hz (UFLS first stage)
stress_scenarios_not_probabilistic.use: design basis (statement of intent, not observed)

limitations: Table lists unit-trip/load-loss events; system-collapse conditions (Uri) are missing, so true extremes are NOT in the data

Nadir depth for a given MW loss fell ~11%/yr (t=-16.7) over 2018-2025 (faster/more frequency response); the model holds the latest-year response fixed: it does not extrapolate the trend and assumes the response persists; a legacy-response (2019) sensitivity is provided
Stage 2 explains ~60% of nadir variance with the year term; response timing and event type remain unmodeled
Nadir levels below ~59.7 Hz (observed minimum) are extrapolated; rates there have very wide CIs and depend on the tail model
Reporting thresholds (dF>=60 mHz or >=350 MW) truncate small events; Poisson rate assumes independent events
Inertia in these reports is a system estimate; future inertia/IBR levels may differ
